text: The Patriots put together perhaps their most dominant performance of the season in a 45-17 demolition of the Raiders on Sunday, with Drake Maye recording five total touchdowns and delivering what film review suggests was his best outing yet—all the more impressive given that New England was without multiple starters, including their top receiver and both starting cornerbacks. Maye appears to have found his confidence and rekindled his deep ball in the process, a particularly encouraging development considering the injury concerns mounting around him as the season progresses. The victory came at a cost, however: running back TreVeyon Henderson left the game with an ankle injury, while left tackle Will Campbell suffered what sources told NFL Network is believed to be a knee sprain, putting two key offensive pieces in question heading forward. Still, Head Coach Mike Vrabel's squad demonstrated considerable resilience and execution in cruising past Las Vegas, proving they can win big games even when their depth gets tested.
